description: The MCP tools Uncut gives the agent (Claude Code, Codex, ACP agents). Modules add their own agentTools (e.g. argent_record) on top. Every edit goes through timeline_edit, so it is checked, undoable per turn and attributed.

tools.name: project_read
tools.description: Read the project. 'summary' gives tracks, items with start and length, scenes, media and the revision; 'full' gives project.json. Long videos: pass a range.
tools.returns: revision, duration, and the project summary or full JSON

tools.name: timeline_edit
tools.description: Apply edit ops atomically. Pass the revision you last read; if the user changed the same items since then, the edit is refused and you get the user's changes. One call is one undo step inside your turn.

summary.description: One line the user sees in the turn card, e.g. 'Cut the shaky parts of the ridge shot'.

tools.returns: the new revision, or a conflict with the user's newer edits, or validation errors

tools.name: render_frames
tools.description: Render frames of the current edit exactly as export would, and return them as images to look at.

tools.name: contact_sheet
tools.description: One image with a grid of frames, each captioned with its frame and time: from a media file (pulled from the original) or from the edit (drawn as the export draws it). Much cheaper than many render_frames when scanning footage for the good parts. 'every' samples every N frames; without it, 'max' frames (default 24) are spread evenly. 'at: shots' (with media) shows one frame per shot (the middle of each), from the video analysis (run now if needed, cached after). At most 60 cells.

media.description: A media id from project_read. Frames and range are then in project frames of that media (like an item's in).

range.description: Frames [start, end): of the edit, or of the media when media is given. Default: all of it.

every.description: Frames between samples when at is 'every'.

max.description: Most cells (default 24 when every isn't given).

tools.returns: one JPEG (at most 1600 px wide) and, as text, the frame and time of every cell in order (with at: shots, each shot's frames too); at: shots while the analysis still runs: { video: { state: running | queued }, note } (call again)

tools.name: media_analyze
tools.description: Analyse a media file. 'loudness' (also 'silence'): integrated loudness (LUFS), loudness range, true peak and the silences (below -40 dB for at least 0.3 s). 'video' (also 'shots', 'motion', 'stability'): cuts, frozen stretches and, per second, stability (no camera shake), sharpness, exposure and a cleanScore 0-1, with the best stretch inside one shot. Frames in the answer are usable as in. Runs on demand and waits up to about a minute; if the answer says running, call again with the same arguments (it joins the job). Results are cached in .cache/ by the file's content, so asking twice is free. 'transcript': the speech transcribed on this Mac (a summary: language, word, filler and pause counts; transcript_read gives the words). Beats and description come later.

analyzers.description: Which analyses (default: loudness with silences; name video to get it, it takes longer). silence = loudness; shots, motion, stability = video.

range.description: Only list silences, cuts, frozen stretches and per-second scores overlapping these project frames of the media [start, end). The measurement is always of the whole file.

tools.returns: per analyzer (loudness, video, transcript): { state: done | running | queued | failed | cancelled, ... }; loudness when done: { cached, hasAudio, seconds, integratedLufs, loudnessRangeLu, truePeakDbtp, silence: { thresholdDb, minSeconds, count, ranges: [{ start, end, startSeconds, endSeconds }] } }; video when done: { cached, hasVideo, seconds, sourceFps, cleanScore, stability, sharpness, exposure, frozen, measures: { shakePercent, panPerSecond, blur, brightness }, best: { start, end, startSeconds, endSeconds, cleanScore, ... }, shots, cuts: { threshold, count, list: [{ frame, seconds, score }] }, frozen: [{ start, end, startSeconds, endSeconds }], drops: [{ frame, seconds, missingSeconds }], stretches: [{ start, end, quality: good | fair | poor, cleanScore }], perSecond: { firstSecond, cleanScore: [], stability: [], sharpness: [], exposure: [], panPerSecond: [] } } (frames are project frames of the media); transcript when done: { cached, hasAudio, seconds, language, model, words, segments, fillers: { hesitation, maybe }, pauses, pauseSeconds, opening }

tools.name: media_rank
tools.description: Rank video takes by how clean they are: cleanScore 0-1 from stability (no camera shake beyond smooth pans), sharpness (in focus) and exposure, with frozen stretches counted against it. Each take comes with its components (to explain the choice) and its best stretch: the cleanest window seconds inside one shot, as project frames usable as in. Runs or joins the video analysis (cached by content, so asking again is free) and waits up to about a minute; takes still being analysed come back under pending: call again with the same arguments.

media.description: Media ids from project_read. Default: the media imported from folder, or all the project's video.

folder.description: An absolute folder path: rank the project's media whose files are in it (import them first with media_import). Not together with media.

by.description: What to rank by: clean (default, the whole take's cleanScore), best (its best stretch's cleanScore), or one component.

window.description: Length of the best stretch in seconds (default 5).

tools.returns: { by, ranked: [{ rank, media, name, cached, seconds, cleanScore, stability, sharpness, exposure, frozen, measures: { shakePercent, panPerSecond, blur, brightness }, shots, drops, best: { start, end, startSeconds, endSeconds, cleanScore, stability, sharpness, exposure, frozen } }], pending?: [{ media, state, progress }], failed?, skipped?, note }

tools.name: transcript_read
tools.description: What's said in a media file, transcribed on this Mac with whisper.cpp (language detected; pass language to force one): text lines with word indices and frames, or each word with its frames; fillers and pauses (at least 0.3 s, aligned to the silences when the loudness analysis is cached) are marked and listed. Paged: pass from = next.from for more. The first call for a file runs the transcription (and the very first one downloads the speech model) and waits up to about a minute; if it answers running, call again with the same arguments. Cached afterwards by the file's content.

range.description: Only words overlapping these project frames of the media [start, end).

format.description: text (default): one line per sentence, 'w<first word index> [start–end] words', {fillers} and (pause n s) inline. words: each word with start and end frames.

from.description: The first word index to list (next.from of the previous page).

language.description: The spoken language as a code (en, pl, ...), or auto (default: detect). A cached transcript in another language is redone.

tools.returns: { media, state, cached, language, model, seconds, words (total), segments, shown: { from, to }, text (format text) | list: [{ i, text, start, end, unsure?, filler? }] (format words), fillers: [{ i, n, text, start, end, kind: hesitation | maybe }], pauses: [{ start, end, startSeconds, endSeconds, after, edge?, silent? }], next?: { from } } or { transcript: { state: running | queued, progress, stage? } } (frames are project frames of the media)

tools.name: transcript_edit
tools.description: Cut by text: remove words (ranges of transcript_read's word ids), pauses (at least min seconds) and/or hesitation fillers (um, uh, yyy, eee; never the 'maybe' ones) of a media file from every main-track clip that uses it, as one edit on your turn (Undo turn reverts it). Respects each clip's in, length and speed; the main track closes up, items on other tracks don't move. Cuts snap to frames and keep a couple of frames next to the words that stay; adjacent cuts merge; words no longer in the edit are skipped with a note. dryRun returns the plan without changing anything. Gets the transcript like transcript_read (it may have to be made first: if it answers running, call again).

media.description: A media id from project_read; may be left out when exactly one media with sound is on the main track.

remove.description: Word ranges to cut, both ends included, e.g. [{"from": "w12", "to": "w20"}, {"from": "w31"}].

min.description: Pauses at least this many seconds long (default 0.5). A little quiet stays next to each word.

fillers.description: true: also cut the hesitation fillers (English and Polish).

dryRun.description: true: only say what would be cut and the new length.

tools.returns: { media, applied, removed: [{ words?, text, pauses?, fillers?, mediaFrames: { start, end }, frames, seconds, clips }], framesRemoved, secondsSaved, revision, duration, seconds, durationBefore, notes? } (frames: the edit's, mediaFrames: project frames of the media)

tools.name: media_import
tools.description: Add footage, music or images from disk to the project's media. Pass path or paths: a file, a folder (the media files directly inside it, not subfolders), or a list of paths. Files are referenced where they are, never copied or changed. At most 50 files per call. Waits for the import and returns each new media entry with its length, size, fps and whether it has sound, plus what was skipped or failed and why. Undo turn removes what it imported.

path.description: An absolute path (or ~/...) to a file or a folder.

name.description: A display name, for a single file only.

tools.returns: revision, imported: [{ id, kind, name, path, frames, seconds, fps, width, height, hasAudio }], skipped: [{ path, reason }], failed: [{ path, message }]

tools.name: generate_media
tools.description: Make an image, video or audio clip with a generator module. The result lands in Media › Generated with its prompt.
tools.returns: the new media id, or a note that the user needs to add an API key

tools.name: modules_list
tools.description: Installed modules (transitions, text styles, components, effects…) with their params schema, so you know what you can use and how.

tools.name: ui_show
tools.description: Point the user at something in the editor: move the playhead to a frame, select an item (the timeline and Inspector follow) and/or open a panel. Use it to show a result, e.g. the playhead on the cut you made with that clip selected. Later also to walk the user through doing an edit (D5).

select.description: The id of one timeline item (the editor selects one item at a time).

panel.description: Left: media, text, elements (backgrounds), audio. Right: inspector, agent (this chat).
